newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: MANUEL SAYS SAFRICAN ECONOMIC FUNDAMENTALS SOUND.
newsitem.headline: MANUEL SAYS SAFRICAN ECONOMIC FUNDAMENTALS SOUND.

text.p: South African Foreign Minister Trevor Manuel told foreign diplomats on Thursday he was unconcerned about the level of the rand because the country's economic fundamentals are sound.
"The fundamentals of this economy are sound," he told a cocktail party in Cape Town organised by the Western Cape branch of the African National Congress.

"Whatever the fears and doubts people might have had before, today ... is the day we could get up in parliament and reflect on 12 months of sound fiscal management," he said, referring to the adjustment budget address he made earlier in the day.

"Twelve months ago we were sitting very pretty because 12 months ago today it was 3.65 rand to the dollar. On February 16 last year all that changed," he said, referring to the sharp decline in the currency that began on that date.
"But 12 months ago some of our feelings, some of the bright smiles we wore were masks for the number of doubts we had about the shaping of the fundamentals.
"That's gone now, the fears are gone," Manuel said. "We're sitting at a different level of the currency but we are convinced the fundamentals of this economy are sound and can carry us through."

"We're about 80 cents weaker on the rand than we were last year but the fundamentals are much stronger, we're more confident about the ability to use this country as a platform for exports," Manuel said.
